model.method: SCS curve-number rainfall excess from MRLC NLCD land cover and USDA SSURGO hydrologic soil groups, routed by D8 into per-sink catchment ponding over an expanded DEM context domain

d8_runoff_routing.method: D8 steepest-descent catchment routing and per-sink ponding
d8_runoff_routing.limitations: D8 routes each cell to one downslope neighbor; per-sink ponding is a static catchment approximation, not a time-dependent hydraulic simulation. Flat cells use a deterministic index tie-break. Basin overflow is counted as outflow, not routed into downstream basins.

curve_number_summary.curve_number_basis: NRCS TR-55-style curve numbers associated with NLCD land-cover classes and SSURGO hydrologic soil groups; class mappings are generalized, not locally calibrated.
curve_number_summary.landcover_interpolation: bilinearly averaged class fractions from the 30-meter NLCD grid; fine cells are interpolations, not new observations
curve_number_summary.soil_group_interpolation: bilinearly interpolated hydrologic group, then interpolated curve numbers between adjacent soil groups

notes: This is a screening scenario, not an observed or locally calibrated street-flood forecast.

The depth model routes runoff down a D8 terrain network and balances volume within each interior sink catchment; it does not simulate time-dependent hydraulics, streets, pipes, culverts, or lake exchange.
The DEM is expanded beyond the output bbox to include nearby terrain; the returned contours are clipped back to the requested bbox.
30-meter NLCD classes and sparse SSURGO soil samples are interpolated for the finer terrain grid; interpolation adds no new source observations.
USGS gage stage is reported as context only and is not transferred from a distant gage to the local flood surface.
Groundsource event footprints are recent historical event evidence, not point-depth labels and are not used to fit a depth predictor.
Contour rings are simplified to at most 15 coordinates, including the closing coordinate; holes are omitted by the payload schema.
Mapped surface-water polygons are served separately by /waterbodies and are not encoded as zero-depth flood contours.
Coastal storm-surge products and FEMA hazard zones are not converted to local rainfall depth. Surge needs a coastal boundary condition and compatible datum.
No current local WDFN gage-height observation is available; the most recent daily stage is historical and is not used to compute this estimate.
Groundsource has historical event footprints in this box but no point water-level or depth observations.
NOAA VDatum could not convert this location to LMSL; absolute elevation values remain in the source DEM datum identified in ar_flood_data.

vertical_datum_conversion.error: NOAA VDatum reports no valid transformation at this location.

landcover.interpolation: 30-meter classes are bilinearly averaged to the DEM analysis grid; interpolated pixels are estimates, not new observations

soils.source: USDA NRCS SSURGO Soil Data Access
soils.interpolation: bilinear between the 4x4 sampled soil groups

data_source_roles.usgs_wdfn_v1: Live/cached station and gage observations provide context; unavailable/stale gage data is not extrapolated to the bbox.
data_source_roles.usgs_3dep: Supplies terrain elevations for DEM-based ponding screening.
data_source_roles.groundsource: 2026 historical flood-event footprints provide recent event context and candidate hindcast areas; they contain no depth labels.
data_source_roles.mrlc_nlcd: Land-cover class raster supplies land-surface categories used to select generalized runoff curve numbers.
data_source_roles.usda_ssurgo: Spatially sampled hydrologic soil groups contribute to the runoff curve-number calculation; missing coverage falls back to average group C.
data_source_roles.surface_water: USGS NHD at broader scales and OpenStreetMap in small boxes identify existing waterbody polygons; these are not flood-depth observations.
data_source_roles.fema_nfhl: Not queried by this scenario function; mapped hazard zones must remain a separate hazard-context overlay, not rainfall depth input.
data_source_roles.noaa_storm_surge: Not applied to these inland Gainesville examples. Coastal surge needs a spatial water-level boundary condition and vertical-datum conversion.

groundsource.dataset_title: Groundsource: A Dataset of Flood Events from News

interpretation: The rainfall excess is estimated with a generalized SCS curve-number method using land-cover and soil layers, then routed on a D8 terrain network to static, spill-capped sink catchments. It is not locally calibrated and does not simulate time-dependent drainage or full hydraulic flow; it is not suitable for life-safety decisions.
